findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION Inspector observed raw eggs stored over sliced tomatoes, pre-cooked cabbage, and ice cream condiments in the prep cooler on the cook line. CORRECTED- Proper storage order was reviewed with PIC and the storage order was corrected. Ensure that the appropriate storage order is followed to avoid cross contamination between raw and ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Multiple food contact surfaces were observed to contain soil accumulation
1) One of the coffee maker internal surface was observed to contain some soil accumulation. CORRECTED- The coffee maker surface was wiped with a clean sanitizer wipe by a staff member.
2) REPEAT: The soda nozzles at the server station were observed to contain soil accumulation. CORRECTED- The soda nozzles were removed to be cleaned and sanitized.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the faucets at the mop sink and the wash sink under the potatoes chopper to be leaking. Ensure the above mentioned sinks are repaired by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The accumulation of grease buildup was observed between and under the equipments such as the grill and fryers along the cook line. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the relevant cleaning will be done. Ensure that frequently used equipments are routinely cleaned to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed food handler wash hands, and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. CORRECTED- education was provided about the need to use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. During hand washing, ensure that soap is applied after water, hands are washed for a minimum of 20 seconds, and then a clean barrier is used to turn off the faucet.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.comment:
Multiple food contact surfaces were observed to contain soil accumulation
1) The ice baffles were observed to contain some soil accumulation. CORRECTED- The ice baffles were wiped with a clean sanitizer wipe by the person in charge.
2) The soda nozzles at the server station were observed to contain soil accumulation. CORRECTED- The soda nozzles were removed to be cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- Inspector observed food debris in the following locations:
1) The potato chopper located on the prep wall in the kitchen. CORRECTED- the potato chopper was removed from the wall to be cleaned and sanitized by the person in charge.
2) Two knives in ready-to-use storage on the magnetic strip of the prep wall in the kitchen.  CORRECTED- Both knives were removed; one knife was damaged but voluntarily discarded by the person in charge

Ensure all food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspectors observed two unlabeled containers of white powder stored under the prep table in the back of the kitchen. CORRECTED- Inspector notified the person in charge of the unlabeled containers, and the labeling was corrected. Ensure that all white powders not in their original container are labeled with their common name to avoid confusion.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple large gaps along the perimeter of the back door. Person in charge communicated to the inspectors that the facility plans to reinstall the door. Ensure that the door is tight fitting to prevent entry of pests into the facility by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two wet sanitizing wiping cloths being stored on the kitchen prep counter. CORRECTED- education was provided about the storage of sanitizing wipes between uses. Ensure sanitizer cloths are stored in a sanitizer solution when they are not in use.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed plates in ready to use position being stored face up under acoustic tiles to the left of the microwave. Inspector informed person in charge (PIC) that food contact surfaces must be inverted or covered to protect from potential contaminants. CORRECTED- PIC inverted plates. Ensure that food contact surfaces are placed under a covering or inverted.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.[C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the faucet at the mop sink to be leaking. Ensure mop sink is repaired by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in the facility to be in need of repair:
1) Holes were observed along the wall behind the server station and on the south wall across from the dish machine.
2) The shelving unit across from the dish machine contains a visible gap between the shelf and wall. Since the shelf is immobile, it needs sealed to the wall. Secure and caulk the shelving unit to the wall.
3) The double sink prep wall next to the standing prep cooler (the one holding the pancake and waffle batter) appears fragmented. Re-caulk the sink to the wall.
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed with a drink on the cook line without straw and lid. An employee was also observed using their cellphone with their gloves on. CORRECTED- Inspector interrupted the employee using a cellphone and reminded them to wash hands and change gloves before returning to work. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are educated to wash their hands and change their gloves after touching other items that may cause contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and:(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed raw fish stored over cooked gumbo in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Proper storage order was reviewed with PIC and the storage order was corrected. Ensure that the appropriate storage order is followed to avoid cross contamination between raw and ready-to-eat foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The following food contact surfaces were observed to have accumulated food debris:
1. Ladles and an egg slicer on the hanging rack above the 2 compartment sink were observed to have the accumulation of soil.
2. A utensil with damaged handle and accumulated food debris was observed on the rack adjacent to the cook line.
3. Blender cups used for crepes were observed with food debris inside.
CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and the utensil with the damaged handle was discarded. The other items were taken to be cleaned. Ensure that food debris is fully cleaned from utensils in the warewashing process before returning them to clean equipment storage. While in constant use, food contact surfaces needed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: An open half-gallon of chocolate milk in the front counter vertical cooler had passed the manufacturer’s printed date and without any in-house date marking. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and the chocolate milk was voluntarily discarded. Foods must be labeled with the date they are opened to ensure they are used or discarded within 7 days of opening. Ensure that the manufacturer’s printed dates of food items are monitored at a regular frequency to avoid spoilage or contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an unlabeled container of white powder stored under the prep table in the back of the kitchen. Discussed with PIC and the labeling was corrected. Ensure that all white powders not in its original container is labeled with their common name to avoid confusion.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a knife being stored hanging in the gap between another table and the prep table on the cook line. PIC was made aware of the appropriate storage of utensils during food preparation and the knife was taken away. Ensure that in-use utensils are always stored properly to avoid the contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The accumulation of grease buildup was observed between and under the equipments along the cook line. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the relevant cleaning will be done. Ensure that frequently used equipments are routinely cleaned to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Food handler training certificate was not available for one of the employees working during this inspection. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed. Keep food handler certificates on file in the facility for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Employee observed handling a slice of raw onion for a hamburger with bare hands. Since this was being added to a plate for service, this onion is a ready-to-eat food. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed glove use and bare-hand contact with PIC and employees. Ensure gloves or utensils are used to handle ready-to-eat foods.
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs were observed stored on top of ready-to-eat foods (cheese, tomatoes, etc) in the top of the prep cooler. CORRECTED- Raw shell eggs were moved to the walk-in cooler. Discussed storing eggs in the cooler below or, during busy periods, on the counter using Time as a Control.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Ice cream scoop was observed in a cup of dirty water above the ice cream freezer. Per staff, no ice cream has been served today. CORRECTED- PIC removed the scoop and discarded the water. Scoop was washed, rinsed, and sanitized, before being returned to the area in a container of clean water. During slow periods, wash, rinse, and sanitize the ice cream scoop after each use. Discussed creation of a time as a control policy (using a timer) to ensure the water is changed at least every 4 hours.
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned at least every 4 hours. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
1) A container of cooled rice was observed without date-marking in the front under-counter cooler. CORRECTED- PIC added a date label to indicate the day the rice was prepared.
2) A container of portioned cooked chicken was observed with two date-labels, both more than 7 days past (7/1 and 7/3). CORRECTED- PIC relabeled the container to indicate the actual date prepared. Ensure all foods are labeled with the date prepared, and that foods are used or discarded within 7 days.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
One wet wiping cloth was observed stored on the waffle iron counter. CORRECTED- Cloth was moved to be stored in the sanitizer bucket. Ensure wet wiping cloths are stored submerged in sanitizer between uses.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: The 3 compartment sink is not sealed to the wall. Replace caulking at the triple sink.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The caulk along the edge of the back handsink is cracked and damaged. Replace caulking so it is smooth and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]
